persona: Independent simulated beginner, first introduction to RILL, interested in a short relaxed lo-fi sketch.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Visible prompts led from an empty area to an instrument and MIDI editor. Pencil drawing, duplication, trimming, naming and both exports were possible by mouse. Precise trimming and naming took corrections.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark teal arrangement, clear waveforms and small MIDI previews looked cohesive and readable. The instrument library had a plain placeholder image, and the native save dialog looked visually separate.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Note drawing and clip duplication responded promptly. WAV export showed progress and completed during this short session. Screenshot/tool overhead and the virtual audio environment prevent a performance benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Mostly clear after trying controls. Scrolling the tempo field had no visible effect. Duplicate became a tool requiring a clip click. The first MIDI trim ended at 30.134 seconds and needed a small corrective drag.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The tested workflow included audio, a VST instrument, a MIDI piano roll, arrangement editing, project naming/saving and WAV/MIDI export. This is a good set for the requested sketch; broader production features were not evaluated.

findings.observation: Clicked the displayed 112 BPM field and scrolled down; it remained 112 BPM. Continued at that tempo. The adjacent minus/plus controls were visible but not used.
The empty-area prompt said double-click for MIDI. Doing so opened the device library; Assign instrument created a new track and pattern with Rill Lab Sine shown on the track.
Double-clicking the pattern opened the piano roll. Pencil drags created visible notes with lengths and pitch labels, and drawing beyond the original end extended the clip.
Clicking Duplicate selected a tool and displayed Click a clip to duplicate. Subsequent clip clicks produced adjacent copies. Zooming out exposed the growing arrangement.
Dragging the final clip edges shortened the arrangement, but the first MIDI trim left 0:30.134 in the title. A small second drag changed it to 0:30.000.
After Play, the position changed from the start to 004.02.26, the yellow playhead moved and both track meters lit. Stop returned it to the start. No audio was auditioned.

Rename project exposed a Keyboard button with clickable letters. A mistyped sodt rain was visible in the save dialog. Cancel, rename, Clear and more letter clicks corrected it to soft rain, and the save dialog inherited that filename.

WAV export displayed Arrangement 0:30 plus tails. Unchecking Include effect tails changed it to 0:30. Confirming the native dialog started a visible progress indicator and then an Exported soft rain.wav success notice.
Export MIDI opened a native dialog with soft rain.mid in the same session folder. Confirming it produced an Exported soft rain.mid success notice.

The first screenshot immediately after opening Save showed a black native-dialog region; the next screenshot showed a usable dialog. The dialog was at the upper left. No operation failed because of this.

outcome.status: Completed in the visible UI: named and saved a 30-second arrangement with audio plus MIDI through Rill Lab Sine, and saw successful WAV and MIDI exports. Files require independent verification.
outcome.composition: 112 BPM, 4/4. Reused the supplied Circuit rhythm audio and drew a six-note MIDI phrase. Duplicated both four-bar clips into four adjacent sections and trimmed the last section to two bars for fourteen bars total. Simple repeating sketch; its audible lo-fi character was not verified.
outcome.playback_observed: Play became Pause, the transport advanced to 004.02.26, the yellow playhead moved and both audio and instrument track meters lit. Stopped playback afterward.

limitations: No file contents or heard audio claim; independent coordinator verification follows. Artifact paths are from the visible native dialogs and selected names.
Only screenshots and mouse input were used to compose. No keyboard events, shortcuts, source inspection, project-state APIs or direct composition-file edits.
The laboratory virtual audio backend and software graphics do not establish physical-device latency, audible quality or general performance.
Only the installed Rill Lab Sine VST3 was used; other third-party plug-ins and advanced production workflows were not evaluated.
